Logo nos primeiros anos ele notou o ciclo das estações, que tem cerca de 6 ppm (partes por milhão) de amplitude: o CO2 chega ao máximo em maio, cai na primavera e no verão do Norte, quando as plantas novas o retiram do ar pela fotossíntese, chega ao mínimo em setembro e sobe de novo quando as folhas caem e apodrecem. O hemisfério Norte domina essa respiração porque concentra a maior parte das terras e, portanto, da vegetação. Por baixo das ondas, a curva sobe sem parar: eram 313 ppm em março de 1958. No começo dos anos 1960, a Fundação Nacional de Ciência dos EUA cortou o apoio à pesquisa, que considerou "rotineira". Hoje é o registro contínuo de CO2 mais longo do mundo. Segundo a NOAA, a média global de 2024 foi de 422,8 ppm, um recorde, e a última vez que o CO2 esteve tão alto foi há cerca de 3 milhões de anos.

fontes.trecho: The Keeling Curve is a graph of the annual variation and overall accumulation of carbon dioxide in the Earth's atmosphere based on continuous measurements taken at the Mauna Loa Observatory on the island of Hawaii from 1958 to the present day. [...] Keeling obtained funding from the Weather Bureau to install infrared gas analyzers at remote locations, including the South Pole and on the volcano of Mauna Loa on the island of Hawaii. Mauna Loa was chosen as a long-term monitoring site due to its remote location far from continents and its lack of vegetation. [...] Keeling's Tellus article of 1960 presented the first monthly CO2 records from Mauna Loa and Antarctica (1957 to 1960), finding a "distinct seasonal cycle [...] show a steady increase in mean atmospheric CO2 concentration from 313 parts per million by volume (ppm) in March 1958 [...] The Keeling Curve also shows a cyclic variation of about 6 ppm each year corresponding to the seasonal change in uptake of CO2 by the world's land vegetation. Most of this vegetation is in the Northern Hemisphere, where most of the land is located. From a maximum in May, the level decreases during the northern spring and summer as new plant growth takes CO2 out of the atmosphere through photosynthesis. After reaching a minimum in September, the level rises again in the northern fall and winter as plants and leaves die off and decay, releasing CO2 back into the atmosphere.

In the early 1960s, the National Science Foundation stopped supporting his research, calling the outcome "routine". [...] The data collection started by Keeling and continued at Mauna Loa is the longest continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide in the world

fontes.titulo: Climate Change: Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide (NOAA Climate.gov)
fontes.trecho: global average atmospheric carbon dioxide was 422.8 parts per million (“ppm,” for short) in 2024, a new record high. [...] the last time atmospheric carbon dioxide amounts were this high was roughly 3 million years ago

gancho: Nos cilindros de gelo tirados da Antártida, o ar preso nas bolhas é mais jovem que o gelo em volta. Num dos pontos de coleta, a neve leva uns 2.500 anos para virar gelo e fechar as bolhas.
explicacao: Quando a neve se acumula, cada camada comprime as de baixo, que viram firn, um material intermediário e ainda poroso, por onde o ar continua circulando. Só quando a densidade chega a cerca de 830 kg por metro cúbico o firn vira gelo e o ar fica selado em bolhas, guardando a composição da atmosfera daquele momento. Na Groenlândia e na Antártida, isso acontece entre 64 e 115 metros de profundidade. Onde neva muito, é rápido: no Summit Camp, na Groenlândia, o gelo se fecha aos 77 metros, com 230 anos. Em Dome C, na Antártida, onde neva pouco, são 95 metros e 2.500 anos. Por isso, ao comparar o CO2 das bolhas com a temperatura registrada no próprio gelo, os cientistas precisam calcular essa diferença de idade. Mais fundo, por volta de 1.500 metros, a pressão empurra as moléculas de ar para dentro dos cristais de gelo, as bolhas somem e o gelo fica mais transparente. O mesmo pouco acúmulo de neve que atrasa o fechamento faz o registro de Dome C ir tão longe: chega a 800 mil anos.

fontes.trecho: As snow accumulates, each layer presses on lower layers, making them denser until they turn into firn. Firn is not dense enough to prevent air from escaping; but at a density of about 830 kg/m3 it turns to ice, and the air within is sealed into bubbles that capture the composition of the atmosphere at the time the ice formed. The depth at which this occurs varies with location, but in Greenland and the Antarctic it ranges from 64 m to 115 m. Because the rate of snowfall varies from site to site, the age of the firn when it turns to ice varies a great deal. At Summit Camp in Greenland, the depth is 77 m and the ice is 230 years old; at Dome C in Antarctica the depth is 95 m and the age 2500 years. As further layers build up, the pressure increases, and at about 1500 m the crystal structure of the ice changes from hexagonal to cubic, allowing air molecules to move into the cubic crystals and form a clathrate. The bubbles disappear and the ice becomes more transparent. [...] The Dome C core had very low accumulation rates, which mean that the climate record extended a long way; by the end of the project the usable data extended to 800,000 years ago.

fontes.titulo: New constraints on the gas age-ice age difference along the EPICA ice cores, 0–50 kyr (Climate of the Past, 2007)
fontes.trecho: Gas is trapped in polar ice sheets at ~50–120 m below the surface and is therefore younger than the surrounding ice. Firn densification models are used to evaluate this ice age-gas age difference (Δage) in the past.

gancho: Entre 717 e 635 milhões de anos atrás, a Terra pode ter congelado quase inteira. Um cientista soviético calculou que, se isso ocorresse, ela nunca mais descongelaria. A saída teriam sido os vulcões.
explicacao: A hipótese da "Terra bola de neve" vem de rochas deixadas por geleiras em lugares que, pelo magnetismo registrado nelas, estavam nos trópicos. Os episódios principais são dois, entre cerca de 717 e 635 milhões de anos atrás. Nos anos 1960, o climatologista Mikhail Budyko mostrou com um modelo simples que, se o gelo avançasse o bastante a partir dos polos, o brilho dele refletiria tanta luz solar que o planeta esfriaria mais, até congelar todo. Mas concluiu que isso nunca tinha acontecido, porque o modelo não oferecia saída. Em 1992, Joseph Kirschvink, que cunhou o nome, propôs uma: com a superfície coberta, as rochas param de reagir com a água e de retirar CO2 do ar, enquanto os vulcões continuam soltando o gás. Ao longo de 4 a 30 milhões de anos, o CO2 chegaria a algo como 350 vezes o nível atual, cerca de 13% da atmosfera, até derreter o gelo nos trópicos. Ainda se discute se a Terra congelou inteira ou se sobrou uma faixa de mar aberto perto do equador, e há quem conteste a própria ideia de um congelamento global.

fontes.trecho: The Snowball Earth is a geohistorical hypothesis proposing that during one or more of Earth's icehouse climates, the planet's surface was nearly entirely frozen, with little or no liquid water exposed. This global glaciation hypothesis is most commonly associated with the Cryogenian Period, which included two major glacial episodes: the Sturtian (c. 717–660 Ma) and Marinoan (c. 650–635 Ma). [...] Opponents of the hypothesis contest the geological evidence for global glaciation [...] Several unanswered questions remain, including whether Earth was a full "snowball" or a "slushball" with a thin equatorial band of open (or seasonally open) water. [...] In the 1960s, Mikhail Budyko, a Soviet climatologist, developed a simple energy-balance climate model to investigate the effect of ice cover on global climate. Using this model, Budyko found that if ice sheets advanced far enough out of the polar regions, a feedback loop ensued where the increased reflectiveness (albedo) of the ice led to further cooling and the formation of more ice, until the entire Earth was covered in ice and stabilized in a new ice-covered equilibrium. While Budyko's model showed that this ice-albedo stability could happen, he concluded that it had, in fact, never happened, as his model offered no way to escape from such a feedback loop. [...] he presented palaeomagnetic data showing that glacial tillites in Svalbard and Greenland were deposited at tropical latitudes. [...] The term "snowball Earth" was coined by Joseph Kirschvink in a short paper published in 1992 [...] the introduction of a mechanism by which to escape from a completely ice-covered Earth—specifically, the accumulation of CO2 from volcanic outgassing leading to an ultra-greenhouse effect. [...] The snowball Earth hypothesis was originally devised to explain geological evidence for the apparent presence of glaciers at tropical latitudes. [...] The carbon dioxide levels necessary to thaw Earth have been estimated as being 350 times what they are today, about 13% of the atmosphere. Since Earth was almost completely covered with ice, carbon dioxide could not be withdrawn from the atmosphere by release of alkaline metal ions weathering out of siliceous rocks. Over 4 to 30 million years, enough CO2 and methane, mainly emitted by volcanoes but also produced by microbes converting organic carbon trapped under the ice into the gas, would accumulate to finally cause enough greenhouse effect to make surface ice melt in the tropics

gancho: Preso como inimigo no início da Primeira Guerra, logo depois de casar, o sérvio Milutin Milanković abriu a mala na cela e voltou às contas que ligariam as eras glaciais às variações da órbita da Terra.
explicacao: Milanković casou em junho de 1914 e, a caminho da lua de mel na Suíça, passou pela aldeia natal, Dalj, então parte da Áustria-Hungria. Ali soube do assassinato de Francisco Ferdinando. Como era oficial da reserva do exército sérvio, foi detido e levado a um campo de prisioneiros. Na primeira noite, tirou da mala seus artigos e anotações sobre o "problema cósmico" e escreveu até passar da meia-noite. Seu mentor, Emanuel Czuber, conseguiu que ele passasse o cativeiro em Budapeste com direito a trabalhar, e lá ele ficou quase toda a guerra, estudando na biblioteca da Academia de Ciências. A ideia central é que mudanças lentas na forma da órbita, na inclinação e na direção do eixo da Terra redistribuem a luz do Sol entre estações e latitudes, o bastante para marcar o ritmo das eras glaciais. A obra que reuniu quase três décadas de cálculos foi para a gráfica em 2 de abril de 1941, quatro dias antes do bombardeio de Belgrado, que destruiu a gráfica; quase todas as folhas já impressas escaparam no depósito. Os ciclos que ele calculou foram confirmados, embora sua teoria original seja hoje vista como incompleta.

fontes.trecho: Milankovitch married Kristina Topuzović, an amateur opera singer, on 14 June 1914. They decided to go on their honeymoon to Switzerland, but before that they stopped in Milankovitch's native village of Dalj in Austria-Hungary, where they heard that Franz Ferdinand had been assassinated in Sarajevo [...] Milankovitch was soon arrested by the Austro-Hungarian authorities because he was a reserve officer in the Royal Serbian Army and at first he spent six weeks under house arrest, but was eventually imprisoned and later sent to a prisoner-of-war camp [...] In the suitcase  I had my printed works and my notes on the cosmic problem, there was clean paper too and I started writing. It was far past midnight when I stopped. [...] Through his social connections, Professor Czuber arranged Milanković's release from prison and permission to spend his captivity in Budapest with the right to work. [...] enabled him to work undisturbed in the Academy's library and the Central Meteorological Institute. Milanković spent four years in Budapest, almost the entire war. [...] rth's orbit that gradually redistribute insolation between the seasons and low- and high-latitude regions (now known as Milankovitch cycles), and he developed a quantitative theory of climate where these insolation cycles were sufficient to cause the recurring ice ages of the Quaternary period. While the Milankovitch cycles in insolation have been confirmed and further substantiated by subsequent research, the classical Milankovitch theory of climate, in its original formulation, provides an incomplete explanation of glacial–interglacial climate dynamics. [...] which covered his nearly three decades of research [...] The manuscript was submitted to print on 2 April 1941 – four days before the attack of Nazi Germany and its allies on the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. In the bombing of Belgrade on 6 April 1941, the printing house where his work was being printed was destroyed; however, almost all of the printed sheet paper remained undamaged in the printing warehouse. [...] almost all of the printed sheet paper remained undamaged in the printing warehouse

The Earth's orbit varies between nearly circular and mildly elliptical (its eccentricity varies). [...] In addition, the tilt of the Earth's axis (its obliquity) changes slightly. [...] Finally, the direction in the fixed stars pointed to by the Earth's axis changes (axial precession)

gancho: Há uns 12.900 anos, quando a Terra saía da última era glacial, o frio voltou de repente. Em poucas décadas, a Groenlândia ficou até 10 °C mais fria. A época leva o nome de uma flor.
explicacao: O episódio se chama Dryas Recente e durou até uns 11.700 anos atrás. O nome vem da Dryas octopetala, uma flor da tundra alpina cujos fósseis são abundantes nos sedimentos escandinavos dessa época. No período quente anterior, a planta era rara, e havia árvores na Escandinávia. O resfriamento atingiu o Atlântico Norte em poucas décadas, com 2 a 6 °C a menos na Europa e cerca de 3 °C a menos na América do Norte. Enquanto isso, o hemisfério Sul esquentou. Esse efeito de gangorra é a pista da causa: o consenso é que houve um enfraquecimento forte da grande circulação de correntes do Atlântico, que leva calor do sul para o norte. O que provocou esse enfraquecimento ainda é debatido. A hipótese mais tradicional é uma enxurrada de água doce e fria de um lago gigante de degelo na América do Norte, e uma erupção vulcânica também foi proposta. O fim foi tão brusco quanto o começo, com um aquecimento forte em cerca de 50 anos, que marca a passagem para a época atual, o Holoceno.

fontes.trecho: The Younger Dryas (YD, Greenland Stadial GS-1) was the final climatic phase of the Last Glacial Period that occurred from around 12,900 to 11,700 years Before Present [...] It is primarily known for the sudden or abrupt cooling in the Northern Hemisphere, when the North Atlantic Ocean cooled and annual air temperatures decreased by around 3 °C (5 °F) over North America, 2–6 °C (4–11 °F) in Europe and up to 10 °C (18 °F) in Greenland, in a few decades. Cooling in Greenland was particularly rapid, taking place over just 3 years or less. At the same time, the Southern Hemisphere experienced warming. This period ended as rapidly as it began, with dramatic warming over around 50 years, the transition from the glacial Pleistocene epoch into the current Holocene interglacial. [...] This "polar seesaw" pattern is consistent with changes in thermohaline circulation (particularly the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation or AMOC), which greatly affects how much heat is able to go from the Southern Hemisphere to the North. [...] The scientific consensus is that severe AMOC weakening explains the climatic effects of the Younger Dryas. [...] However, there is some debate over what caused the AMOC to become so weak in the first place. The hypothesis historically most supported by scientists was an interruption from an influx of fresh, cold water from North America's Lake Agassiz into the Atlantic Ocean. [...] A volcanic eruption as an initial trigger for cooling and sea ice growth has been proposed more recently [...] The Younger Dryas period is named after the alpine–tundra wildflower Dryas octopetala, because its fossils are abundant in the European (particularly Scandinavian) sediments dating to this timeframe. [...] On the contrary, Dryas octopetala was rare during the Bølling–Allerød Interstadial. Instead, European temperatures were warm enough to support trees in Scandinavia

gancho: Até uns 5 a 6 mil anos atrás, boa parte do Saara tinha capim, árvores e lagos. O lago Chade ficou ao menos dez vezes maior que hoje e foi o maior lago da Terra. Havia hipopótamos e crocodilos onde hoje é deserto.
explicacao: É o chamado Período Úmido Africano, que começou há cerca de 14.500 anos. A causa principal foram mudanças lentas no eixo da Terra, que fortaleceram as monções africanas, reforçadas pela própria vegetação, pela redução da poeira e por mais gases de efeito estufa. No auge, o "Megachade" chegou a 1.000 por 600 quilômetros. Fósseis mostram uma fauna de savana e de rio: elefantes, girafas, rinocerontes, hipopótamos, crocodilos, pelicanos e peixes como a perca-do-nilo. Pessoas caçavam, coletavam e criavam gado, cabras e ovelhas onde hoje quase nada vive, e deixaram pinturas como as da Caverna dos Nadadores, nas montanhas de Gilf Kebir, no Egito, com cenas de gente nadando. Foram essas pinturas em lugares hoje inóspitos que levaram exploradores a propor um Saara verde, ideia que ganhou nome nos anos 1930. Quando o período acabou, as populações foram migrando para lugares com água garantida, como o vale do Nilo e a Mesopotâmia. O período úmido marcou fundo as culturas africanas, inclusive o nascimento da civilização egípcia. E simular um Saara tão verde ainda é um desafio para os modelos climáticos.

fontes.trecho: The African humid period (AHP; also known by other names) was a climate period in Africa during the late Pleistocene and Holocene geologic epochs, when North Africa was wetter than it is today. The covering of much of the Sahara by grasses, trees, and lakes was caused by changes in the Earth's axial tilt, changes in vegetation and dust in the Sahara which strengthened the African monsoon, and increased greenhouse gases. [...] The humid period began about 14,600–14,500 years ago [...] The AHP ended 6,000–5,000 years ago [...] The AHP led to the widespread settlement of the Sahara and the Arabian Desert and had a profound effect on African cultures, including the birth of the Ancient Egyptian civilization. People in the Sahara lived as hunter-gatherers and domesticated cattle, goats, and sheep. [...] rock paintings such as those in the Cave of Swimmers and in the Acacus Mountains. Earlier humid periods in Africa were postulated after the discovery of these rock paintings in now-inhospitable parts of the Sahara. When the period ended, humans gradually abandoned the desert in favour of regions with more secure water supplies, such as the Nile Valley and Mesopotamia [...] Further discoveries of petroglyphs led desert explorer László Almásy to coin the concept of a Green Sahara in the 1930s. [...] in general, the simulation of the Green Sahara is considered a problem for Earth system models. [...] This fauna included antelopes, baboons, birds, cane rats, catfish, clams, cormorants, crocodiles, elephants, frogs, gazelles, giraffes, hartebeest, hares, hippopotamuses, molluscs, Nile perches, pelicans, rhinoceroses [...] Scenes include animals and everyday life such as swimming which supports the presence of past wetter climates. One well-known such petroglyph location is the Cave of Swimmers in the Gilf Kebir mountains of Egypt [...] The largest of them was Lake Chad which increased to at least ten times its present-day size to form Lake Megachad or Megalake Chad, then the largest lake on Earth. This enlarged Lake Chad reached dimensions of 1,000 by 600 kilometres

gancho: Há uns 49 milhões de anos, uma samambaia aquática pode ter florescido no oceano Ártico por 800 mil anos e, ao afundar, ajudado a tirar CO2 do ar e a esfriar o planeta. É a hipótese do "evento Azolla".
explicacao: Alguns milhões de anos antes, a Terra tinha passado por uma fase de estufa, com calor bastante para tartarugas e palmeiras nos polos. O Ártico era um mar quase fechado, com uma camada de água doce dos rios boiando sobre a água salgada, e bastavam alguns centímetros dela para a Azolla, uma samambaia de água doce, se espalhar. Com calor moderado e até 20 horas de sol, ela pode dobrar de massa em dois ou três dias. As plantas mortas afundavam num fundo sem oxigênio, onde nada as decompunha, e acabavam enterradas. Em sedimentos de toda a bacia do Ártico, perfurações acharam uma camada de pelo menos 8 metros com finíssimas lâminas de Azolla fossilizada. O episódio coincide com uma queda forte do CO2 do ar, e a hipótese é que a samambaia tenha contribuído para ela, ao lado de outros fatores, ajudando a virar o clima de estufa para o de gelo nos polos que vivemos hoje. Há céticos: as plantas podem ter sido levadas ao mar por correntes, vindas de deltas e lagoas. Esses depósitos também atraem interesse da indústria do petróleo.

fontes.trecho: The Azolla event is a paleoclimatology scenario hypothesized to have occurred in the middle Eocene epoch, around 49 million years ago, when blooms of the carbon-fixing freshwater fern Azolla are thought to have happened in the Arctic Ocean. As the fern died and sank to the stagnant sea floor, it were incorporated into the sediment over a period of about 800,000 years; the resulting draw-down of carbon dioxide has been speculated to have helped reverse the planet from the "greenhouse Earth" state of the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum, when the planet was hot enough for turtles and palm trees to prosper at the poles, to the current icehouse Earth known as the Late Cenozoic Ice Age. [...] In sedimentary layers throughout the Arctic basin, a unit reaching at least 8 m in thickness [...] switch with millimetre-thick laminations comprising fossilised Azolla matter. [...] The event coincides precisely with a catastrophic decline in carbon dioxide levels, which fell from 3500 ppm in the early Eocene to 650 ppm during this event. [...] The plant can grow at great speed in favourable conditions – modest warmth and 20 hours of sunlight, both of which were in evidence at the poles during the early Eocene – and can double its biomass over two to three days in such a climate. [...] During the early Eocene, the continental configuration was such that the Arctic Sea was almost entirely cut off from the wider oceans. [...] This low-density freshwater formed a nepheloid layer, floating on the surface of the dense sea. Even a few centimetres of fresh water would be enough to allow colonization by Azolla [...] The anoxic bottom of the Arctic basin, a result of the stratified water column, permitted just this; the anoxic environment inhibits the activity of decomposing organisms and allows the plants to sit unrotted until they are buried by sediment. [...] even by very conservative estimates more than enough carbon could be sequestered by plant burial to account for the observed 80% drop in CO2 by this one phenomenon alone. Other factors almost certainly played a role. [...] skeptical scientists point out that it would be possible for Azolla colonies in river deltas or freshwater lagoons to be swept into the Arctic Ocean by strong currents [...] Much of the current interest in oil exploration in the Arctic regions is directed towards the Azolla deposits

gancho: Nos anos 1960, uma base militar dos EUA escavada no gelo da Groenlândia tirou um tubo de solo de baixo de mais de um quilômetro de gelo. Esquecido num freezer, ele guardava folhas e musgo de uns 416 mil anos atrás.
explicacao: A base era Camp Century, escavada em túneis no gelo e movida a reator nuclear. Oficialmente era uma estação científica, mas servia de teste para o Projeto Iceworm, que pretendia esconder centenas de mísseis nucleares sob o gelo, perto da União Soviética. Os mísseis nunca foram instalados. Os cientistas de lá perfuraram o gelo até a base e, no fim, tiraram também um tubo de terra e rocha de baixo dele. Mas estavam interessados no gelo, não na terra. O material foi de um freezer militar para a Universidade de Buffalo nos anos 1970, e de lá para um freezer na Dinamarca nos anos 1990, onde se perdeu. Foi reencontrado por acaso em 2017, e dentro havia folhas e musgo, restos de uma paisagem sem gelo. Um estudo publicado em 2023 na revista Science, que datou o sedimento pela luminescência dos grãos, concluiu que o lugar estava livre de gelo há cerca de 416 mil anos, com margem de uns 38 mil, num período quente parecido com o atual. O derretimento da época teria elevado o nível do mar em pelo menos cinco pés, cerca de um metro e meio. Para os autores, o gelo da Groenlândia é mais sensível ao aquecimento do que se pensava.

fontes.titulo: Greenland Melted Recently, Shows Higher Risk of Sea Level Rise (University of Vermont)
fontes.trecho: During the Cold War, a secret U.S. Army mission, at Camp Century in northwestern Greenland, drilled down through 4560 feet of ice on the frozen island—and then kept drilling to pull out a twelve-foot-long tube of soil and rock from below the ice. Then this icy sediment was lost in a freezer for decades. It was accidentally rediscovered in 2017 and shown to hold not just sediment but also leaves and moss, remnants of an ice-free landscape, perhaps a boreal forest. [...] An international team of scientists was amazed to discover that Greenland was a green land only 416,000 years ago (with an error margin of about 38,000 years). Their new study was published in the journal Science on July 21, 2023. [...] This indicates that the ice sheet on Greenland may be more sensitive to human-caused climate change than previously understood [...] The new study presents direct evidence that sediment just beneath the ice sheet was deposited by flowing water in an ice-free environment during a moderate warming period called Marine Isotope Stage 11, from 424,000 to 374,000 years ago. This melting caused at least five feet of sea level rise around the globe. [...] At Rittenour’s lab, sediment from the Camp Century core was examined for what is called a “luminescence signal.” [...] Camp Century was a military base hidden in tunnels under the Greenland ice sheet in the 1960s. One strategic purpose of the camp was a top-secret operation, called Project Iceworm, to hide hundreds of nuclear missiles under the ice near the Soviet Union. As cover, the Army claimed the camp was an Arctic science station. [...] The Camp Century scientists were focused on the ice itself [...] They took little interest in the twelve feet of sediment gathered from beneath their ice core. Then, in a bizarre story, the ice core was moved in the 1970s from a military freezer to the University at Buffalo—and then to another freezer in Denmark in the 1990s. [...] a long interglacial with temperatures similar to or slightly warmer than today.
Missiles were never fielded at the facility [...] It consisted of 21 tunnels with a total length of 9,800 feet (3.0 km) and was powered by a nuclear reactor.

gancho: Diz-se que nos anos 1970 os cientistas previam uma nova era do gelo. Algumas revistas falaram nisso, mas, entre os estudos da época sobre o clima do século XXI, menos de 10% apontavam para esfriamento.
explicacao: A origem do mito está em reportagens como a da revista Newsweek de abril de 1975, "The Cooling World", que falava em sinais de que o planeta caminhava para o frio. Havia um fato por trás: a temperatura média do hemisfério Norte tinha caído um pouco desde os anos 1940. Hoje há consenso de que a causa principal foi a própria poluição, porque a queima de combustíveis lançava partículas de enxofre que refletem a luz do Sol. Mas a literatura científica da época estava mais preocupada com o aquecimento pelo efeito estufa, e a maior parte dos artigos que olhavam para o século XXI previa aquecimento. Em 1959, a revista Science News já estimava que o CO2 do ar subiria 25% entre 1850 e 2000; o aumento real foi de 29%. Em junho de 1976, a Organização Meteorológica Mundial alertou que um aquecimento muito significativo era provável. Quando o esfriamento chegou à imprensa, a temperatura já tinha parado de cair, e depois voltou a subir com força. Em 2006, mais de 31 anos depois, a Newsweek publicou uma correção admitindo ter errado "de forma espetacular" sobre o futuro próximo.

fontes.trecho: Some press reports in the 1970s speculated about continued cooling; these did not accurately reflect the scientific literature of the time, which was generally more concerned with warming from an enhanced greenhouse effect. An overall warming trend from the late Industrial Revolution did slow and reverse slightly from the 1940s to the 1970s due to high industrial emissions of sulfur-based aerosols, but then continued sharply upward into the 2020s. [...] In the scientific papers which considered climate trends of the 21st century, fewer than 10% were inclined towards future cooling, while most papers predicted future warming. [...] but Science News in May 1959 forecast a 25% increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide in the 150 years from 1850 to 2000, with a consequent warming trend. The actual increase in this period was 29%. [...] By the time the idea of global cooling reached the public press in the mid-1970s temperatures had stopped falling, and there was concern in the climatological community about carbon dioxide's warming effects. In response to such reports, the World Meteorological Organization issued a warning in June 1976 that "a very significant warming of global climate" was probable. [...] there is now general agreement that aerosol effects were the dominant cause of the mid-20th century cooling. [...] An April 28, 1975, article in Newsweek magazine was titled "The Cooling World", it pointed to "ominous signs that the Earth's weather patterns have begun to change" [...] On October 23, 2006, Newsweek issued a correction, over 31 years after the original article, stating that it had been "so spectacularly wrong about the near-term future" [...] The average surface air temperature in the northern hemisphere increased from the 1880s until about 1940 and has been decreasing thereafter.

gancho: Desde 1950, o pH da superfície do oceano caiu só de cerca de 8,15 para 8,05. Parece pouco, mas a escala de pH é logarítmica: isso equivale a uns 26% a mais de íons de hidrogênio, que é o que mede a acidez.
explicacao: O mar absorve parte do CO2 que a humanidade emite: cerca de 30% das emissões desde o começo da era industrial. Na água, o gás forma ácido carbônico, que se desfaz e libera íons de hidrogênio, e são eles que baixam o pH. Como a escala é logarítmica, uma unidade de pH corresponde a dez vezes mais íons, e por isso um décimo já pesa tanto. Apesar do nome "acidificação", a água do mar ainda é alcalina, com pH acima de 8: o que muda é a direção. O problema é sobretudo para quem constrói concha ou esqueleto de carbonato de cálcio, como corais, moluscos e pequenos caramujos nadadores, os pterópodes, que estão na base da cadeia alimentar do Ártico e cujas conchas se dissolvem com mais acidez. Algo parecido já aconteceu no passado da Terra. O ritmo atual costuma ser comparado ao do aquecimento de 56 milhões de anos atrás, na passagem do Paleoceno para o Eoceno, que provocou uma grande extinção de organismos do fundo do mar. Só que hoje o carbono entra no sistema atmosfera-oceano cerca de dez vezes mais depressa que naquela época.

fontes.trecho: CO2 from the atmosphere is absorbed by the oceans. This chemical reaction produces carbonic acid (H2CO3) which dissociates into a bicarbonate ion (HCO−3) and a hydrogen ion (H+). The presence of free hydrogen ions (H+) lowers the pH of the ocean, increasing acidity (this does not mean that seawater is acidic yet; It is still alkaline, with a pH higher than 8). Marine calcifying organisms, such as mollusks and corals, are especially vulnerable because they rely on calcium carbonate to build shells and skeletons. [...] Ocean acidification has happened before in Earth's geologic history. [...] as a result of the uptake of approximately 30% of the anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions over the past 270 years (since around 1750). [...] Between 1950 and 2020, the average pH value of the ocean surface is estimated to have decreased from approximately 8.15 to 8.05. This represents an increase of around 26% in hydrogen ion concentration in the world's oceans (the pH scale is logarithmic, so a change of one in pH unit is equivalent to a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration). [...] Current rates of ocean acidification have been likened to the greenhouse event at the Paleocene–Eocene boundary (about 56 million years ago), when surface ocean temperatures rose by 5–6 °C. In that event, surface ecosystems experienced a variety of impacts, but bottom-dwelling organisms in the deep ocean actually experienced a major extinction. Currently, the rate of carbon addition to the atmosphere-ocean system is about ten times the rate that occurred at the Paleocene–Eocene boundary. [...] Pteropods and brittle stars both form the base of the Arctic food webs and are both seriously damaged from acidification. Pteropods shells dissolve with increasing acidification

gancho: Quando a Terra era jovem, o Sol brilhava só uns 70% do que brilha hoje. Pelas contas, o planeta deveria estar congelado, mas tinha água líquida e vida. Como isso foi possível ainda é debatido.
explicacao: O problema foi levantado pelos astrônomos Carl Sagan e George Mullen em 1972. O Sol fica mais brilhante com a idade: a fusão no núcleo transforma hidrogênio em hélio e reduz o número de partículas, o núcleo se contrai e esquenta, e a fusão acelera. Modelos indicam que hoje ele é 1,4 vez mais brilhante do que há 4,6 bilhões de anos. Sagan e Mullen sugeriram que a amônia teria aquecido a Terra primitiva, mas esse gás é destruído com facilidade pela luz solar. A explicação mais aceita hoje é que havia muito mais CO2 no ar, mantido por um termostato natural: quando o planeta esfria, chove menos, as rochas se desgastam menos e param de retirar CO2, que se acumula até reaquecer tudo, num ciclo de centenas de milhares de anos. As contas indicam que seria preciso ao menos 0,1 bar de CO2 para manter a superfície acima do congelamento. Mas a quantidade real de CO2 da época ainda é discutida, e uma análise de minerais de ferro de rochas antigas sugeriu que micróbios produtores de metano também podem ter ajudado a aquecer. E o papel das nuvens e do brilho da superfície continua sendo uma das grandes incertezas.

fontes.trecho: The faint young Sun paradox or faint young Sun problem describes the apparent contradiction between observations of liquid water early in Earth's history and the astrophysical expectation that the Sun's output would have been only 70 percent as intense during that epoch as it is during the modern epoch. The paradox is this: with the young Sun's output at only 70 percent of its current output, early Earth would be expected to be completely frozen, but early Earth seems to have had liquid water and supported life. The issue was raised by astronomers Carl Sagan and George Mullen in 1972. Proposed resolutions of this paradox have taken into account greenhouse effects, changes to planetary albedo, astrophysical influences, or combinations of these suggestions. The predominant theory is that the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide contributed most to the warming of the Earth. [...] The brightening is caused by a decrease in the number of particles per unit mass due to nuclear fusion in the Sun's core, from four protons and electrons each to one helium nucleus and two electrons. Fewer particles would exert less pressure. A collapse under the enormous gravity is prevented by an increase in temperature, which is both cause and effect of a higher rate of nuclear fusion. [...] More recent modeling studies have shown that the Sun is currently 1.4 times as bright today as it was 4.6 billion years ago [...] Sagan and Mullen suggested during their descriptions of the paradox that it might be solved by high concentrations of ammonia gas, NH3. However, it has since been shown that while ammonia is an effective greenhouse gas, it is easily destroyed photochemically in the atmosphere [...] In particular, during a time of low surface temperatures, rainfall and weathering rates would be reduced, allowing for the build-up of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere on timescales of 0.5 million years. Specifically, using 1-D models [...] scientists have determined that at 4.5 Ga, with a 30% dimmer Sun, a minimum partial pressure of 0.1 bar of CO2 is required to maintain an above-freezing surface temperature [...] The amount of carbon dioxide is still under debate. [...] Then in 2010, Rosing et al. analyzed marine sediments called banded iron formations and found large amounts of various iron-rich minerals [...] Anaerobic, single-celled organisms that produced methane (CH4) may therefore have contributed to the warming in addition to carbon dioxide. [...] Clouds continue to be the dominant source of uncertainty in 3-D global climate models

gancho: Na Pequena Idade do Gelo, Londres fazia feiras sobre o Tâmisa congelado; na última, em 1814, um elefante atravessou o rio. Mas o frio não explica tudo: a velha London Bridge ajudava a represar o rio.
explicacao: A maior parte dessas feiras aconteceu entre o começo do século XVII e o começo do XIX, quando os invernos britânicos eram mais rigorosos. Mesmo assim, eram raras: de 1400 até 1831, o rio congelou em Londres em 24 invernos. A mais célebre foi a do Grande Frio de 1683-84, quando o Tâmisa ficou totalmente congelado por dois meses, com gelo de 28 centímetros. Havia corrida de cavalos e carruagens, patinação, teatro de bonecos e um impressor que vendia cartões com o nome do freguês e a prova de que foram impressos sobre o rio; o rei Carlos II comprou um. A geografia ajudava: sem margens construídas, o rio era mais largo e lento. E os 19 pilares da ponte medieval, protegidos por grossas caixas de madeira que foram crescendo com os anos, estreitavam os arcos. No inverno, pedaços de gelo se prendiam ali, fechavam os vãos e faziam a ponte agir como uma represa. Depois de 1814, o clima foi ficando mais ameno, a ponte foi demolida em 1831, substituída por outra de arcos largos, e o rio ganhou margens construídas ao longo do século XIX. Nunca mais houve feira.

fontes.trecho: Most were held between the early 17th and early 19th centuries during the period known as the Little Ice Age, when the river froze over most often, though still infrequently. During that time the British winter was more severe than it is now, and the river was wider and slower, further impeded by the 19 piers of the medieval Old London Bridge which were removed in 1831. [...] From 1400 until the removal of the medieval London Bridge in 1831, there were 24 winters in which the Thames was recorded to have frozen over at London. [...] During the Great Frost of 1683–84, the most severe freeze recorded in England, the Thames was completely frozen for two months, with the ice reaching a thickness of 11 inches (28 cm) in London. [...] The Thames was broader and shallower in the Middle Ages – it was yet to be embanked, meaning that it flowed more slowly. Moreover, old London Bridge, which carried a row of shops and houses on each side of its roadway, was supported on many closely spaced piers; these were protected by large timber casings which, over the years, were extended – causing a narrowing of the arches below the bridge, thus concentrating the water into swift-flowing torrents. In winter, large pieces of ice would lodge against these timber casings, gradually blocking the arches and acting like a dam for the river at ebb tide. [...] Activities included horse and coach racing, ice skating, puppet plays and bull-baiting [...] For sixpence, the printer Croom sold souvenir cards written with the customer's name, the date, and the fact that the card was printed on the Thames; he was making five pounds a day (ten times a labourer's weekly wage). King Charles II bought one. [...] The frost fair of 1814 began on 1 February, and lasted four days, between Blackfriars Bridge and London Bridge. An elephant was led across the river below Blackfriars. [...] This was the last frost fair. The climate was growing milder; old London Bridge was demolished in 1831 and replaced with a new bridge with wider arches, allowing the tide to flow more freely; and the river was embanked in stages during the 19th century, all of which made the river less likely to freeze.

gancho: O gelo da Antártida registra uma queda do CO2 do ar no fim do século XVI e começo do XVII. Um estudo de 2019 atribui boa parte dela às florestas que cresceram nas Américas depois que epidemias mataram 90% dos indígenas.
explicacao: A queda foi de 7 a 10 ppm, maior que a margem de erro das medições, com o mínimo no começo do século XVII. A explicação mais citada liga a queda à chegada dos europeus. Pesquisadores do University College London reuniram 119 estimativas regionais e calcularam que as Américas tinham cerca de 60,5 milhões de habitantes antes de 1492. No século seguinte, epidemias trazidas pelos europeus mataram cerca de 90% deles. Roças e áreas manejadas foram abandonadas e a vegetação voltou a crescer em 55,8 milhões de hectares, retirando carbono do ar. Pelas contas do estudo, isso explicaria uma queda de 3,5 ppm e, somados outros efeitos, de 47% a 67% da queda total. O período coincide com um esfriamento global de cerca de 0,15 °C, e os autores sugerem que a mortandade pode ter contribuído para a fase mais fria da Pequena Idade do Gelo. Há explicações naturais concorrentes, e as estimativas têm margens largas. A queda, chamada de "Orbis spike", foi proposta por alguns cientistas como marco do início do Antropoceno, a época em que a humanidade passou a alterar o planeta, mas a ideia é disputada.

fontes.titulo: Earth system impacts of the European arrival and Great Dying in the Americas after 1492 (Quaternary Science Reviews, 2019)
fontes.trecho: Geography, University College London [...] Available online 25 January 2019 [...] From 1 19 published regional population estimates we calculate a pre-1492 CE population of 60.5 million [...] European epidemics removed 90% [...] of the indigenous population over the next century. This resulted in secondary succession of 55.8 Mha [...] of abandoned land [...] equivalent to a decline in atmospheric CO 2 of 3.5 ppm [...] 47 e67% of the atmospheric CO 2 decline. [...] may have reduced atmospheric CO 2 levels and led to a decline in radiative forcing that may then have contributed to the coldest part of the Little Ice Age [...] This analysis shows that the cooling over this period was 0.15 +C.

The Orbis Spike is a global dip in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels around the year 1610 CE, as recorded by the Antarctic sea ice record. There are several hypotheses as to what caused the dip, the chief among them being diseases brought by European explorers. [...] There has been controversy raised about whether the Orbis Spike should be recognized as the beginning of the Anthropocene [...] The levels of carbon dioxide decreased by an estimated 7-10ppm, which is higher than the 1-2ppm that is the usual margin of error for such measurements. While it is certain that atmospheric carbon dioxide decreased at this time, the exact mechanisms responsible for this drop are debated.

gancho: Pelas estimativas do IPCC, mesmo que o aquecimento pare em 1,5 °C, o mar seguirá subindo por séculos: 2 a 3 m nos próximos 2.000 anos. Se parar em 2 °C, 2 a 6 m; com 5 °C de aquecimento, 19 a 22 m.
explicacao: Os números estão no Sumário para Formuladores de Políticas do sexto relatório do IPCC, de 2021. A razão é a inércia: as águas profundas do oceano continuam esquentando e as grandes camadas de gelo seguem derretendo, num processo lento. Por isso, segundo o relatório, o nível do mar está comprometido a subir por séculos a milênios e ficará elevado por milhares de anos, com alta confiança. Já os números exatos para os próximos 2.000 anos são classificados pelo próprio relatório como de baixa confiança, pela incerteza sobre o comportamento das camadas de gelo. Mesmo tirando mais CO2 do ar do que se emite, levaria séculos a milênios para essa subida se inverter. Neste século, a alta é bem menor e depende do cenário: até 2100, em relação a 1995-2014, a faixa provável vai de 0,28 a 0,55 m no cenário de emissões muito baixas e de 0,63 a 1,01 m no de emissões muito altas. O passado ajuda a conferir as projeções longas. Há cerca de 125 mil anos, com temperaturas de 0,5 a 1,5 °C acima do nível pré-industrial, o mar provavelmente estava de 5 a 10 m acima do atual. Há uns 3 milhões de anos, com 2,5 a 4 °C a mais, ficava de 5 a 25 m acima.

fontes.titulo: IPCC AR6 WGI: Summary for Policymakers (2021)
fontes.trecho: IPCC, 2021: Summary for Policymakers. [...] B.5.3  It is virtually certain that global mean sea level will continue to rise over the 21st century. Relative to 1995–2014, the likely  global mean sea level rise by 2100 is 0.28–0.55 m under the very low GHG emissions scenario (SSP1-1.9) [...] 0.63–1.01 m under the very high GHG emissions scenario (SSP5-8.5) [...] B.5.4  In the longer term, sea level is committed to rise for centuries to millennia due to continuing deep-ocean warming and  ice-sheet melt and will remain elevated for thousands of years (high confidence). Over the next 2000 years, global mean  sea level will rise by about 2 to 3 m if warming is limited to 1.5°C, 2 to 6 m if limited to 2°C and 19 to 22 m with 5°C of  warming [...] likely 5–10 m higher than  today around 125,000 years ago, when global temperatures were very likely 0.5°C–1.5°C higher than 1850–1900; and very  likely 5–25 m higher roughly 3 million years ago, when global temperatures were 2.5°C–4°C higher (medium confidence). [...] it would take several centuries to millennia for global mean sea level to reverse  course even under large net negative CO2 emissions (high confidence). [...] and it will continue to rise over subsequent millennia ( low confidence)

gancho: Em 1992, um contêiner com 28.800 brinquedos de banho caiu no Pacífico Norte. Oceanógrafos transformaram os patos, castores, tartarugas e sapos de plástico num grande experimento sobre correntes.
explicacao: Em 10 de janeiro de 1992, uma tempestade perto da Linha Internacional de Data derrubou doze contêineres de um navio que ia de Hong Kong para Tacoma, nos EUA. Um deles levava 28.800 Friendly Floatees, brinquedos sem furos, que não se enchem de água. A embalagem de papelão se desfez no mar e eles ficaram livres. Os oceanógrafos Curtis Ebbesmeyer e James Ingraham, de Seattle, viram ali uma chance rara: o método usual era soltar de 500 a 1.000 garrafas à deriva, e no Pacífico só cerca de 2% dos objetos costumam ser recuperados. Dez meses depois, os primeiros brinquedos apareceram no Alasca, a uns 3.200 km do ponto de partida, e até agosto de 1993 foram achados 400 na costa leste do Golfo do Alasca. Cada achado alimentou um modelo de computador das correntes de superfície, que acertou a previsão de novas chegadas ao estado de Washington em 1996. Os pesquisadores previram ainda que parte dos brinquedos passaria pelo Estreito de Bering, ficaria presa no gelo do Ártico e levaria anos para chegar ao Atlântico Norte. Com o tempo, sol e água salgada desbotaram patos e castores até o branco, enquanto tartarugas e sapos mantiveram as cores.

fontes.trecho: departed from Hong Kong on a container ship, the Evergreen Ever Laurel, destined for Tacoma, Washington. On 10 January 1992, during a storm in the North Pacific Ocean close to the International Date Line, twelve 40-foot (12-m) intermodal containers were washed overboard. One of these containers held 28,800 Floatees, a child's bath toy which came in a number of forms: red beavers, green frogs, blue turtles and yellow ducks. [...] subsequent tests showed that the cardboard quickly degraded in sea water allowing the Floatees to escape. Unlike many bath toys, Friendly Floatees have no holes in them so they do not take on water. Seattle oceanographers Curtis Ebbesmeyer and James Ingraham, who were working on an ocean surface current model, began to track their progress. The mass release of 28,800 objects into the ocean at one time offered significant advantages over the standard method of releasing 500–1000 drift bottles. The recovery rate of objects from the Pacific Ocean is typically around 2% [...] Ten months after the incident, the first Floatees began to wash up along the Alaskan coast. The first discovery consisted of ten toys found by a beachcomber near Sitka, Alaska on 16 November 1992, about 3,200 kilometres (2,000 mi) from their starting point. [...] in total 400 were found along the eastern coast of the Gulf of Alaska in the period up to August 1993. [...] the oceanographers correctly predicted further landfalls of the toys in Washington state in 1996 and theorized that many of the remaining Floatees would have traveled to Alaska, westward to Japan, back to Alaska, and then drifted northwards through the Bering Strait and become trapped in the Arctic pack ice. Moving slowly with the ice across the Pole, they predicted it would take five or six years for the toys to reach the North Atlantic [...] Bleached by sun and seawater, the ducks and beavers had faded to white, but the turtles and frogs had kept their original colors.

gancho: Ondas gigantes que surgem do nada já foram tratadas como lenda de marinheiro. Em 1º de janeiro de 1995, um laser numa plataforma do Mar do Norte mediu uma de 25,6 m, mais que o dobro das vizinhas.
explicacao: Relatos de marinheiros e estragos em navios sugeriam havia muito tempo que essas ondas existiam, mas faltavam provas sólidas, e elas chegaram a ser consideradas míticas. A plataforma Draupner, uma estrutura de apoio a gasodutos a cerca de 160 km da ponta sul da Noruega, tinha sido projetada para aguentar a onda calculada para um evento de uma vez em 10.000 anos, com altura prevista de 20 m. Trazia um laser apontado para baixo, que media o mar. Em 1º de janeiro de 1995, com ondas de cerca de 12 m ao redor, o aparelho registrou uma de 25,6 m de altura, com a crista a 18,5 m acima do nível da água parada. Os outros sensores confirmaram a leitura, e a plataforma teve danos leves. A onda era mais que duas vezes mais alta e íngreme que as vizinhas, com características fora de qualquer modelo de ondas conhecido, e reforçou a ideia de que ondas assim ocorrem naturalmente. Elas podem surgir quando correntes ou ventos fazem as ondas viajarem em velocidades diferentes e se juntarem numa só, ou quando efeitos não lineares transferem energia entre ondas até formar uma única onda enorme.

fontes.trecho: The wave, determined to be 25.6 m (84 ft) in height, was recorded on 1 January 1995 at Unit E of the Draupner platform, a gas pipeline support complex located in the North Sea about 160 km (100 miles) southwest from the southern tip of Norway. The Draupner platform rig, located in the Norwegian North Sea and 160 km (99 mi) offshore from Norway, was built to withstand a calculated 1-in-10,000-years wave with a predicted height of 20 m (64 ft) and was fitted with state-of-the-art sensors, including a laser rangefinder wave recorder on the platform's underside. [...] The laser beam recorded a rogue wave with a maximum wave height of 25.6 m (84 ft). Peak elevation above still water level was 18.5 m (61 ft). The reading was confirmed by the other sensors. The platform sustained minor damage in the event. In the area, the significant wave height at the time was about 12 m (39 ft), so the Draupner wave was more than twice as tall and steep as its neighbors, with characteristics that fell outside any known wave model. [...] helped solidify the initial speculation that rogue waves did naturally occur

They can be caused when currents or winds cause waves to travel at different speeds, and the waves merge to create a single large wave, or when nonlinear effects cause energy to move between waves to create a single extremely large wave. Once considered mythical and lacking hard evidence, rogue waves are now proven to exist and are known to be natural ocean phenomena. Eyewitness accounts from mariners and damage inflicted on ships have long suggested they occur.

gancho: Em 1868, Thomas Huxley achou no lodo do fundo do Atlântico uma gosma que tomou pela matéria primordial da vida. Era sulfato de cálcio, formado quando a água do mar reagiu com o álcool que conservava a amostra.
explicacao: Huxley reexaminou uma amostra de lama do fundo do Atlântico colhida em 1857 e guardada num pote com álcool. Viu nela um lodo de aspecto albuminoso, cortado por "veias", e o batizou de Bathybius haeckelii, em homenagem a Ernst Haeckel, que imaginava um "lodo primordial" de onde toda a vida teria vindo. Haeckel ficou lisonjeado e escreveu que a substância surgia sem parar no fundo do mar, a partir de matéria sem vida. Em 1870, Huxley chegou a dizer que ela formava um tapete vivo contínuo sobre milhares de milhas quadradas do leito oceânico, provavelmente em volta da Terra toda. Mas a expedição do navio Challenger, iniciada em 1872, passou três anos estudando os oceanos sem achar sinal dela. Em 1875, o químico de bordo, John Young Buchanan, percebeu que a gosma era um precipitado de sulfato de cálcio: a água do mar reagia com o álcool conservante e formava um gel que grudava em partículas como se as engolisse. Huxley admitiu o erro na revista Nature. Haeckel resistiu e defendeu a ideia até 1883. Opositores da evolução usaram o caso como argumento contra a teoria.

fontes.trecho: Bathybius haeckelii was a substance that British biologist Thomas Henry Huxley discovered and initially thought to be a form of primordial matter, a source of all organic life. He later admitted his mistake when it proved to be the product of an inorganic chemical process (precipitation). In 1868, Huxley studied an old sample of mud from the Atlantic seafloor taken in 1857. When he first examined it, he had found only protozoan cells and placed the sample into a jar of alcohol to preserve it. Now he noticed that the sample contained an albuminous slime that appeared to be criss-crossed with veins. Huxley thought he had discovered a new organic substance and named it Bathybius haeckelii, in honor of German biologist Ernst Haeckel. Haeckel had theorized about Urschleim ("primordial slime"), a protoplasm from which all life had originated. [...] Haeckel was impressed and flattered and procured a sample for himself. In the next edition of his textbook, The History of Creation Haeckel suggested that the substance was constantly coming into being at the bottom of the sea, "monera" arising from non-living matter due to "physicochemical causes." Huxley asserted in a speech given to the Royal Geographical Society in 1870 that Bathybius undoubtedly formed a continuous mat of living protoplasm that covered the whole ocean floor for thousands of square miles, probably a continuous sheet around the Earth. [...] In 1872, the Challenger expedition began and spent three years studying the oceans. [...] They did not find any sign of Bathybius, despite the claim that it was a nearly universal substance. In 1875, ship's chemist John Young Buchanan analyzed a substance that looked like Bathybius from an earlier collected sample. He noticed that it was a precipitate of calcium sulfate from the seawater that had reacted with the preservative liquid (alcohol), forming a gelatinous ooze which clung to particles as if ingesting them. [...] He published part of the letter in Nature and recanted his previous views. [...] He continued to support this position until 1883. [...] Other opponents of evolution, including George Campbell, 8th Duke of Argyll, tried to use the case as an argument against evolution.

gancho: Entre a Groenlândia e a Islândia, água gelada desce mais de 3,5 km de altura pelo fundo do mar. Se estivesse em terra, seria a cachoeira mais alta do mundo, com mais de três vezes a altura do Salto Ángel.
explicacao: É o transbordamento do Estreito da Dinamarca, chamado em dinamarquês e norueguês de "bomba da Groenlândia". Ele nasce de uma diferença de densidade: a água que desce dos mares nórdicos é mais fria, e por isso mais pesada, que a do Mar de Irminger, ao sul do estreito. Ao passar pela crista submarina entre a Groenlândia e a Islândia, essa água escorre pelo leito ao longo de cerca de 1.000 km. O fluxo é de cerca de 3,2 milhões de metros cúbicos por segundo, muito acima da descarga do Amazonas no Atlântico. O efeito Coriolis desvia a corrente para a direita, e por isso a água do lado da Groenlândia fica cerca de 1 km mais alta que a do lado oposto do canal. Os oceanógrafos não classificam esses fluxos como cachoeiras, mas a queda supera em mais de três vezes a do Salto Ángel, a maior cachoeira contínua em terra. O transbordamento responde por cerca de metade da água densa que passa dos mares nórdicos para o Atlântico Norte e é peça-chave da circulação termohalina, a rede de correntes profundas que leva calor e substâncias dissolvidas pelo planeta.

fontes.trecho: The Denmark Strait overflow (Danish: Grønlandspumpen; Norwegian: Grønlandspumpa, meaning "the Greenland pump") is an undersea overflow located in the Denmark Strait between Greenland and Iceland. The overflow transports around 3.2 million m3 (110 million ft3) of water per second, greatly eclipsing the discharge of the Amazon River into the Atlantic Ocean [...] The descending column of water [...] descends over a length of around 1,000 km (620 mi). The overflow is formed by the density difference of the water masses either side of the Denmark Strait; the southward-flowing water originating from the Nordic Seas is colder and consequently more dense than the Irminger Sea to the south of the strait. [...] Due to the Coriolis effect, the downward flow of water is deflected to the right, resulting in the descending water on the Greenland side of the channel being roughly 1 km (0.62 mi) higher than the opposite side of the channel. The overflow provides one of the main inflows of North Atlantic Deep Water, accounting for around half of dense water overflow between the Nordic Seas and the North Atlantic. [...] DSOW is a key component of the present-day thermohaline circulation [...] Although undersea overflows are not considered waterfalls, the Denmark Strait overflow would be the tallest waterfall in the world were it on land, with water falling over 3.5 km (2.2 mi); this descent is over three times the height of Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall over land.
The water in these circuits transport energy (as heat) and mass (as dissolved solids and gases) around the globe.

gancho: Depois da Primeira Guerra, o químico Fritz Haber propôs pagar a dívida da Alemanha com ouro tirado do mar. Não deu certo, mas a expedição criada em parte para isso fez um mapa inédito do fundo do Atlântico Sul.
explicacao: Em 1872, o químico E. Sonstadt tinha relatado que os oceanos continham 65 miligramas de ouro por tonelada de água. O Tratado de Versalhes, de 1919, obrigava a Alemanha a pagar em ouro uma enorme dívida de guerra, e Haber sugeriu que o ouro extraído dos mares internacionais podia resolver o problema. Nos anos 1920, ele procurou exaustivamente um método de extração e publicou vários artigos sobre o tema. A conclusão, depois de anos, foi frustrante: a concentração de ouro dissolvido era muito menor que a relatada antes, e a extração não compensava. A expedição alemã do navio Meteor, de 1925 a 1927, teve de início esse objetivo econômico, mas ficou famosa por outro motivo. Equipado com um ecobatímetro, aparelho então recente que mede a profundidade pelo tempo que um pulso sonoro leva para ir ao fundo e voltar, o navio ziguezagueou entre a África e a América do Sul e fez 67.000 sondagens. Foi o primeiro levantamento detalhado do fundo do Atlântico Sul, e ele mostrou que a Dorsal Mesoatlântica, a grande cordilheira submarina do meio do oceano, seguia contínua por todo o Atlântico Sul e continuava até o Oceano Índico.

fontes.titulo: German Expedition Discovers the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (EBSCO Research Starters)
fontes.trecho: The initial purpose of the German Meteor expedition was economic. In 1872, E. Sonstadt reported that the oceans contained a gold concentration of 65 milligrams per metric ton of seawater. The Treaty of Versailles (1919), which ended World War I, required that Germany repay its enormous war debt in gold, and Fritz Haber, a German chemist, proposed that gold extracted from the international seas might solve the problem. [...] An echo sounder works by measuring the time it takes a sonic or ultrasonic pulse emitted by the sounder to reach the object below and then return to the sounder.

In the 1920s, Haber searched exhaustively for a method to extract gold from sea water, and published a number of scientific papers on the subject. After years of research, he concluded that the concentration of gold dissolved in sea water was much lower than that reported by earlier researchers, and that gold extraction from sea water was uneconomic.

The German Meteor expedition (German: Deutsche Atlantik Expedition) was an oceanographic expedition that explored the South Atlantic ocean from the equatorial region to Antarctica in 1925–1927 [...] The ship zigzagged between Africa and South America and took echo soundings of the South Atlantic between 20° North and 60° South. [...] In the course of the venture 67,000 depth soundings were made [...] Meteor was equipped with early sonar equipment with which it produced the first detailed survey of the south Atlantic Ocean floor. The survey established that  the Mid-Atlantic Ridge was continuous through the South Atlantic and continued into the Indian Ocean beyond the Cape of Good Hope.

gancho: Proibida de embarcar por ser mulher, Marie Tharp mapeou o fundo do Atlântico pelas sondagens e achou o vale que indicava a deriva dos continentes. O colega desdenhou: "conversa de menina".
explicacao: Tharp trabalhava no Observatório Geológico Lamont, nos EUA, com o geólogo Bruce Heezen. Ele colhia medidas de profundidade a bordo do navio Vema, e ela as transformava em mapas, porque na época mulheres eram proibidas de trabalhar em navios. Em 1952, alinhando com paciência perfis de sondagem do navio Atlantis, ela notou uma estrutura em V que corria sem interrupção pelo eixo da Dorsal Mesoatlântica e suspeitou que fosse um vale de rifte, aberto pelo afastamento do fundo oceânico. Heezen não se convenceu, porque a ideia apoiava a deriva continental, que muitos cientistas, ele incluído, achavam impossível. A virada veio quando um mapa de epicentros de terremotos no oceano, feito por outro colaborador, foi sobreposto ao perfil dela: os tremores se alinhavam com o vale. Só então Heezen aceitou a hipótese. Na Guerra Fria, o governo americano proibia publicar mapas topográficos do fundo do mar, por medo de que submarinos soviéticos os usassem, e os dois contornaram a regra desenhando o relevo num estilo mais realista. Em 1977, a National Geographic publicou o mapa de todo o fundo oceânico feito por eles. Em 1997, a Biblioteca do Congresso dos EUA incluiu Tharp entre os quatro maiores cartógrafos do século XX.

fontes.trecho: She was hired to perform drafting work with Maurice Ewing, the founder of the Lamont Geological Observatory [...] For the first 18 years of their collaboration, Heezen collected bathymetric data aboard the research ship Vema, while Tharp drew maps from that data since women were barred from working on ships at the time. [...] In 1952, Tharp painstakingly aligned sounding profiles from Atlantis, acquired during 1946–1952 [...] Tharp identified an aligned, v-shaped structure running continuously through the axis of the ridge and believed that it might be a rift valley formed by the oceanic surface being pulled apart. Heezen was initially unconvinced as the idea would have supported continental drift, then a controversial theory. Many scientists, including Heezen, believed that continental drift was impossible at the time. Instead, for a time, he favored the Expanding Earth hypothesis, dismissing her explanation as "girl talk". [...] When Foster's map of earthquake epicenters was overlaid with Tharp's profile of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, it became clear that the location of these earthquakes aligned with Tharp's rift valley. [...] It was only after seeing that the location of earthquake epicenters aligned with Tharp's rift valley that Heezen accepted her hypothesis [...] Because of the Cold War, the U.S. government forbade topographic seafloor maps to be published for fear that Soviet submarines could use them. To circumvent that restriction, Tharp and Heezen decided to draw their maps in a more realistic style [...] their map of the entire ocean floor, which was published in 1977 by National Geographic under the title of The World Ocean Floor. [...] Tharp was recognized in 1997 by the Library of Congress as one of the four greatest cartographers of the 20th century.

gancho: Os navios do correio britânico levavam semanas a mais que os mercantes americanos para cruzar o Atlântico. Benjamin Franklin descobriu o motivo com um primo baleeiro: eles navegavam contra a Corrente do Golfo.
explicacao: Em 1768, na Inglaterra, Franklin ouviu uma queixa curiosa das autoridades alfandegárias. Os paquetes do correio, que partiam de Falmouth, na Cornualha, demoravam semanas a mais para chegar a Nova York do que um navio mercante comum para chegar a Newport, em Rhode Island. E os mercantes saíam de Londres, tendo ainda de descer o Tâmisa e percorrer todo o Canal da Mancha antes de cruzar o oceano. Franklin perguntou ao primo Timothy Folger, capitão baleeiro da ilha de Nantucket. Folger explicou que os mercantes reconheciam a corrente pelo comportamento das baleias, pela temperatura e pela cor da água, e a atravessavam, enquanto os capitães do correio seguiam contra ela. Franklin pediu ao primo que desenhasse o caminho da corrente numa carta do Atlântico, com notas sobre como evitá-la na viagem da Inglaterra para a América, e mandou o mapa ao secretário dos Correios britânicos. A carta foi impressa em Londres em 1769, mas os capitães britânicos em geral a ignoraram. A corrente não era novidade para os navegadores: um resumo do diário de bordo da expedição de Ponce de León, de 1513, já registrava uma corrente mais forte que o vento.

fontes.trecho: A summary of Ponce de León's voyage log on April 22, 1513, noted, "A current such that, although they had great wind, they could not proceed forwards, but backwards and it seems that they were proceeding well; at the end, it was known that the current was more powerful than the wind." [...] In 1768, while in England, Franklin heard a curious complaint from the Colonial Board of Customs: "Why did it take British packets several weeks longer to reach New York from England than it took an average American merchant ship to reach Newport, Rhode Island, despite the merchant ships leaving from London and having to sail down the River Thames and then the length of the English Channel before they sailed across the Atlantic, while the packets left from Falmouth in Cornwall?" Franklin asked his cousin Timothy Folger, a Nantucket Island whaling captain, for an answer. Folger explained that merchant ships routinely crossed the current—which was identified by whale behaviour, measurement of the water's temperature, and changes in the water's colour—while the mail packet captains ran against it. Franklin had Folger sketch the path of the current on a chart of the Atlantic and add notes on how to avoid the current when sailing from England to America. Franklin then forwarded the chart to Anthony Todd, secretary of the British Post Office. Franklin's Gulf Stream chart was printed in 1769 in London, but it was mostly ignored by British sea captains.

gancho: Onde água doce cobre a salgada, um navio pode quase parar, como se algo o segurasse. A "água morta" era tida como lenda de marinheiro até Nansen enfrentá-la em 1893. A culpa é de ondas escondidas sob a superfície.
explicacao: O fenômeno aparece quando uma camada de água doce ou salobra fica sobre água salgada, mais densa, sem que as duas se misturem. É frequente em fiordes onde o degelo das geleiras chega ao mar. Se a camada de cima tem mais ou menos a profundidade do casco, o navio gasta energia criando e mantendo ondas internas na fronteira entre as duas águas. Ele fica difícil de manobrar e pode perder velocidade até quase parar. Em agosto de 1893, num arquipélago perto da Península de Taimir, no Ártico, o explorador norueguês Fridtjof Nansen anotou que o Fram, capaz de 6 a 7 nós com tempo calmo e carga leve, não chegava a 1,5 nó na água morta e nem sempre obedecia ao leme, por mais voltas e manobras que a tripulação tentasse. Nansen pediu ao físico Vilhelm Bjerknes que estudasse o caso, e um aluno dele, Vagn Walfrid Ekman, demonstrou que as ondas internas eram a causa. Acelerar alguns nós pode bastar para escapar. Há ainda uma hipótese histórica curiosa: o efeito pode ter atrapalhado os navios de Cleópatra na Batalha de Áccio, em 31 a.C., derrota que a lenda atribuía a rêmoras grudadas nos cascos.

fontes.trecho: Dead water  is the nautical term for a phenomenon that can occur when there is strong vertical density stratification due to salinity or temperature or both. It is common where a layer of fresh or brackish water rests on top of denser salt water, without the two layers mixing. The phenomenon is frequently, but not exclusively, observed in fjords where glacier runoff flows into salt water without much mixing. [...] In the better known surface phenomenon a ship traveling in a fresh water layer with a depth approximately equal to the vessel's draft will expend energy creating and maintaining internal waves between the layers. The vessel may be hard to maneuver or can even slow down almost to a standstill and "stick". An increase in speed by a few knots can overcome the effect. [...] The phenomenon, long considered sailor's yarns, was first described for science by Fridtjof Nansen, the Norwegian Arctic explorer. Nansen wrote the following from his ship Fram in August 1893 in the Nordenskiöld Archipelago near the Taymyr Peninsula: When caught in dead water Fram appeared to be held back, as if by some mysterious force, and she did not always answer the helm. In calm weather, with a light cargo, Fram was capable of 6 to 7 knots. When in dead water she was unable to make 1.5 knots. We made loops in our course, turned sometimes right around, tried all sorts of antics to get clear of it, but to very little purpose. Nansen's experience led him to request physicist and meteorologist Vilhelm Bjerknes to study it scientifically. Bjerknes had his student, Vagn Walfrid Ekman, investigate. [...] demonstrated the effect of internal waves as being the cause of dead water. [...] An interesting historical possibility is that the effect caused Cleopatra's ships difficulties and loss at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, in which legend attributes the loss to remora (suckerfish) attaching to the hulls.

gancho: O vento não empurra o mar na direção em que sopra. Somando todas as camadas que ele arrasta, a água anda a 90° do vento: para a direita no Hemisfério Norte e para a esquerda no Sul.
explicacao: O vento arrasta por atrito a parte de cima do oceano, entre 10 e 100 m de profundidade. Mas, enquanto a água se move, a rotação da Terra a desvia, pelo efeito Coriolis. Na teoria de Ekman, a superfície corre a 45° do vento (nas medições reais, o ângulo costuma ficar entre 5° e 20°), e cada camada abaixo, puxada pela de cima, fica mais lenta e um pouco mais desviada, num padrão chamado espiral de Ekman. Somando o movimento de toda essa camada, o transporte líquido fica a 90° da direção do vento. A primeira pista veio de Fridtjof Nansen, que percebeu, a bordo do Fram, numa expedição ao Ártico, que o gelo derivava de 20° a 40° à direita do vento predominante. Nansen pediu a Vilhelm Bjerknes que pusesse um aluno no problema, e Vagn Walfrid Ekman apresentou a teoria em 1902, na tese de doutorado. O efeito molda a vida no mar. Na costa do Peru e da Califórnia, onde o vento sopra paralelo ao litoral, a água da superfície é levada para longe da costa e precisa ser reposta por água de baixo. Essa água profunda, fria e rica em nutrientes alimenta florações de fitoplâncton e sustenta algumas das maiores pescarias do planeta.

fontes.trecho: As the wind blows it casts a friction force on the ocean surface that drags the upper 10–100m of the water column with it. However, due to the influence of the Coriolis effect, as the ocean water moves it is subject to a force at a 90° angle from the direction of motion causing the water to move at an angle to the wind direction. [...] the surface current is found to be (as expected) 45 degrees to the right (left) of the wind in the Northern (Southern) Hemisphere. [...] the magnitude of the velocity (the speed) decreases from a maximum at the surface until it dissipates. The direction also shifts slightly across each subsequent layer (right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern Hemisphere). This is called an Ekman spiral. [...] If all flow over the Ekman layer is integrated, the net transportation is at 90° to the right (left) of the surface wind in the Northern (Southern) Hemisphere. [...] Ekman developed the theory of the Ekman layer after Fridtjof Nansen observed that ice drifts at an angle of 20°–40° to the right of the prevailing wind direction while on an Arctic expedition aboard the Fram. Nansen asked his colleague, Vilhelm Bjerknes to set one of his students upon study of the problem. Bjerknes tapped Ekman, who presented his results in 1902 as his doctoral thesis. [...] Upwelling carries nutrient rich, and cold deep-sea water to the euphotic zone, promoting phytoplankton blooms and kickstarting an extremely productive environment. [...] provides the nutrient supply for some of the largest fishing markets on the planet [...] Wind in these regimes blows parallel to the coast (such as along the coast of Peru, where the wind blows out of the southeast, and also in California, where it blows out of the northwest). [...] Because the surface water flows away from the coast, the water must be replaced with water from below. [...] The differences between the theory and the observations are that the angle is between 5–20 degrees instead of the 45 degrees as expected

gancho: A superfície do mar não é lisa. Por causa de diferenças na gravidade, o nível que o oceano teria em repouso fica 106 m mais baixo que a forma de referência da Terra ao sul da Índia e 85 m mais alto perto da Islândia.
explicacao: A massa da Terra não é distribuída por igual, e a gravidade varia um pouco de lugar para lugar. Os geodesistas chamam de geoide a superfície que o oceano teria se tivesse densidade constante e não sofresse com marés, correntes e clima. Ela sobe acima do elipsoide, a Terra "lisa" usada nos cálculos, onde há excesso de massa, e afunda onde há falta. O desvio vai de +85 m, na Islândia, a −106 m, no oceano ao sul da Índia, menos de 200 m no total. A maior depressão é o chamado Baixo do Geoide do Oceano Índico. Comparado ao relevo de terra firme, que vai do Everest, com uns 8.800 m, aos 11.000 m da Fossa das Marianas, o geoide é bem mais suave. Mas o efeito aparece no dia a dia: o GPS mede a altura em relação ao elipsoide, e por isso um receptor sem correção, num navio, pode indicar que o barco sobe e desce durante uma viagem longa, embora ele esteja sempre no nível do mar.

fontes.trecho: Although the "ground" of the Earth has excursions on the order of +8,800 m (Mount Everest) and −11,000 m (Marianas Trench), the geoid's deviation from an ellipsoid ranges from +85 m (Iceland) to −106 m (southern India), less than 200 m total. If the ocean were of constant density and undisturbed by tides, currents or weather, its surface would resemble the geoid. [...] So a GPS receiver on a ship may, during the course of a long voyage, indicate height variations, even though the ship will always be at sea level (neglecting the effects of tides). [...] The surface of the geoid is higher than the reference ellipsoid wherever there is a positive gravity anomaly or negative disturbing potential (mass excess) and lower than the reference ellipsoid wherever there is a negative gravity anomaly or positive disturbing potential (mass deficit). [...] The largest absolute deviation can be found in the Indian Ocean Geoid Low, 106 meters below the average sea level.

gancho: Antes dos computadores eletrônicos, as marés eram previstas por máquinas de polias e engrenagens. Máquinas assim previram as marés do Dia D, e a americana foi mantida em segredo na Segunda Guerra.
explicacao: A maré é a soma de muitos ritmos, ligados aos movimentos da Lua e do Sol, que no conjunto nunca se repetem exatamente. Nos anos 1860, William Thomson, mais tarde Lord Kelvin, introduziu a análise harmônica das marés, que decompõe a curva em componentes regulares. Somar esses termos à mão era trabalhoso e sujeito a erro, e a resposta de Thomson foi mecânica. Na máquina dele, construída em 1872–73, cada componente movia um eixo para cima e para baixo, e uma corrente passava alternadamente por cima e por baixo das polias desses eixos. A ponta livre da corrente somava todos os movimentos e guiava uma caneta que desenhava a curva da maré numa fita de papel. A ideia da corrente foi sugerida pelo engenheiro Beauchamp Tower. Um volante pesado deixava o operador girar a máquina depressa, sem trancos nas polias, e as máquinas de 1876 e 1879 traçavam as marés de um ano para um porto em cerca de quatro horas. Esses computadores analógicos ganharam importância militar nas duas guerras mundiais. A máquina americana No. 2 foi classificada como secreta, junto com os dados que produzia, e serviu para os desembarques em ilhas na Guerra do Pacífico; as marés do Dia D são creditadas a máquinas de latão derivadas do projeto original de Thomson. Os computadores digitais as tornaram obsoletas, mas algumas seguiram em uso até as décadas de 1960 e 1970.

fontes.trecho: A tide-predicting machine was a special-purpose mechanical analog computer of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, constructed and set up to predict the ebb and flow of sea tides and the irregular variations in their heights – which change in mixtures of rhythms, that never (in the aggregate) repeat themselves exactly. Its purpose was to shorten the laborious and error-prone computations of tide-prediction. [...] The first tide-predicting machine, designed and built in 1872–73, and followed by two larger machines on similar principles in 1876 and 1879, was conceived by Sir William Thomson. Thomson had introduced the method of harmonic analysis of tidal patterns in the 1860s [...] Tower suggested the use of a device that (as he remembered) was once used by Wheatstone. It was a chain running alternately over and under a sequence of pulleys on movable shafts. [...] The movements in position of the free (movable) end of the chain represented the sum of the movements of the different shafts. The movable end was kept taut, and fitted with a pen and a moving band of paper on which the pen plotted a tida [...] A flywheel of great inertia enabled the operator to turn the machine fast, without jerking the pulleys, [...] They came to be regarded as of military strategic importance during World War I, and again during the Second World War, when the US No.2 Tide Predicting Machine, described below, was classified, along with the data that it produced, and used to predict tides for the D-Day Normandy landings and all the island landings in the Pacific War.
